recipes.name: Black-Eyed Pea Bratwurst Stew
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds bratwurst sausages, cut into thirds
2 (15 ounce) cans black-eyed peas, rinsed and drained
2 (9 ounce) packages frozen cut green beans, thawed
2 tablespoons hot Buffalo wing sauce (such as Frank's® REDHOT Buffalo Wing Sauce), or to taste
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place bratwurst sausages, black-eyed peas, green beans, potatoes, onion, garlic, chicken stock, Buffalo wing sauce, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, salt, and black pepper in a slow cooker.
Cook on High setting until vegetables are tender and soup is thickened, 3 to 4 hours.
For a thicker stew, whisk flour and water together in a bowl until smooth. Pour mixture into stew and simmer until thickened, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Black-Eyed Pea Bratwurst Stew
raw_recipe.description: Hot wing sauce gives this sausage and black-eyed pea stew a spicy kick.

review.reviewBody: Great flavor! I do think the bratwurst need cut into more manageable pieces. I actually did this in my Instant Pot and it worked great. Saute the onions and brats first, then add everything else, lock the lid and set manual pressure for 15 minutes.

I needed a recipe to use up some sausages I had on hand and I needed a hearty meal to serve the whole family for lunch. No time to cook in the morning so I threw all of this into my crock pot just before bed, left it on low till noon the next day when we served it up with some good bread from a local bakery. Everyone raved over it! 


I used half bratwurst and half Italian sausage because that's what I had on hand. I cut them into 6 pieces each so they'd be a little closer to bite sized. Other than that I did it just as the recipe calls for. Oh, except I stirred the flour into some of the broth and didn't add the extra cup of water.

Made it with no changes to the ingredients, but I cooked in my dutch oven as I got started cooking late in the day and wanted it quicker. Browned the brats, then the veggies and added the brats back in with the rest of the ingredients. Super easy, and quick to assemble. My family loved it. I thought it was pretty tasty. I think I will add a little hot pepper flakes to mine next time. I think it would work with some kind of spicy smoked sausage as well. I might try that next time. Thanks for a great recipe!

Quite good! We used rinsed black beans instead of black eyed peas. This soup is very similar to the Olive Garden Zuppa Toscana, but without all the dairy. Oh, if you cut the fresh bratwurst and remove the casing it will naturally break down in the crock pot, into smaller pieces.
Very good recipe! Great flavor! Easily adjustable in terms of what vegetables you want to add. I added a green and red pepper. My fiancée really enjoys it as well!
What an excellent stew. I did it stove top, because I needed it quicker. I love this recipe and will definitely be making it a lot!!!

Excellent recipe. Different flavors and textures complimentary 

Followed the recipe and was good as is. Might add red and yellow peppers next go around. Did not thicken with flour and probably won't next time. Don't like glowing reviews and am critical of most recipes but this one was an all around winner.

I made this recipe and use a honey baked ham bone!! It was the best and easiest recipe to make! I shared this with my boss and he said he’d had this soups all over with too chefs and this was the recipe ever!! Highly recommend!
Making this for the second time tonight. Yum! I cut the recipe in half for our family of 5.
